title: hosted-api-streaming-postmortem-2025-11-08
content:
Summary:

On 2025-11-08 at ~14:12 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API streaming surface that lasted ~56 minutes (14:12–15:08 UTC). Symptoms: increased tail latency for streaming responses, elevated 5xx rate for streaming endpoints, and multiple client disconnects. Impact: customer-facing streaming sessions experienced interruptions and visible stalls; estimated 18% of active streaming sessions were affected during the window. No data loss reported, but live chat/voice integrations saw partial outages.

Primary customer impact:
- Streaming connections dropped mid-response (client-side errors: ECONNRESET)
- Streaming segments delayed (token emission pauses of 3–20s)
- Non-streaming API (sync text gen) had minor latency blips but remained largely healthy

Detection and timeline (high level):
- 14:10 UTC: synthetic streaming probe (region: us-west2) latency graphs show sporadic stalls (alerts not configured for streaming probes yet)
- 14:12 UTC: PagerDuty p0: high 5xx rate for /v1/stream and 95p latency > 10s triggered (alert rule: streaming-5xx-rate-apex); on-call Eng SRE paged
- 14:15 UTC: Slack incident channel created (#inc-streaming-2025-11-08), triage ongoing. Initial hypothesis: network / LB flapping or upstream model-serving overload
- 14:20 UTC: Preliminary investigation: worker pods on serving-runtime-group-4 showed high read buffer counts and growing RSS memory; kube events show OOMKilled on 3 pods starting at 14:18 UTC (note: OOM, not crashloop)
- 14:28 UTC: Emergency action: scaled serving-runtime-group-4 replica set from 12 -> 24, disabled aggressive request batching for streaming route via feature-flag (--stream-agg=false)
- 14:36 UTC: Partial improvement in error rate, but stalls persisted for new sessions; ongoing stalls for existing in-flight sessions
- 14:45 UTC: Hotfix deployed to revert a runtime change from yesterday that changed stream buffer sizing (roll back to commit 6a3f2c)
- 14:54 UTC: Error rate subsided to baseline; streaming tail latency returned to acceptable SLOs
- 15:08 UTC: All alerts resolved; channel moved to postmortem thread

Root cause (summary):
- A recent runtime change (PR #4577) adjusted streaming buffer allocation logic to pre-allocate larger per-request buffers intended to reduce small-allocation overhead. Under certain request mixes (long-lived low-throughput streaming sessions), this caused memory pressure on the streaming dispatcher workers leading to increased RSS and OOM kills. OOM kills caused traffic redistribution to fewer pods which saturated worker threads and produced head-of-line blocking: queued requests waited for buffer availability, causing streaming stalls and client disconnects (ECONNRESET).

Contributing factors:
- The change was merged without a targeted canary for low-throughput, long-lived streams. CI/unit tests passed but integration/synthetic streaming tests did not cover long tail usage patterns.
- Autoscaling policy relied only on CPU, but the failure mode manifested as memory pressure; the HPA didn't scale quickly because CPU wasn't rising proportionally before pods OOM-killed.
- No synthetic streaming SLO probe existed to detect backpressure on stream token emission rate; only request-level/5xx alerts existed.
- The revert/hotfix path was not pre-documented for streaming buffer config, so early actions were exploratory (trial toggles).

Why this wasn't caught earlier:
- Local dev and unit tests simulate high throughput short streams, not long-lived low-throughput sessions typical of voice assistants and chat continuity.
- Staging traffic did not replicate the customer session mix (few long-lived streams).

Detection/Monitoring gaps (actionable):
- Missing probe: synthetic streaming probe that measures token emission intervals for in-flight sessions.
- Missing metric: per-worker memory reservation/usage exposed to autoscaler as a scaling signal.
- Alert tuning: streaming request error rate alert threshold too coarse; need streaming-specific tail-latency alert.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Scaled replicas to absorb load (12->24) to reduce per-pod queue depth
- Disabled the new stream aggregation/buffer feature flag (--stream-agg=false) to fall back to previous buffer sizing logic
- Rolled back the runtime change to commit 6a3f2c to restore prior allocator behavior (hotfix PR merged and deployed)
- Monitored for OOM events and verified node pressure was cleared

Post-incident root fix plan (short/medium term):
1) Patch allocator to bound per-request pre-allocation with adaptive limits and fall back to pooled small buffer path when memory pressure detected. Owner: Ethan Brooks. ETA: 2025-11-22.
2) Add memory-based autoscaling signal (custom HPA using memory RSS percent) for serving-runtime groups. Owner: Rina Sato. ETA: 2025-11-18.
3) Add synthetic streaming SLO probe that opens a long-lived stream and measures token emission intervals and disconnects across regions. Owner: Samir Patel. ETA: 2025-11-15.
4) Expand CI to run an integration test matrix that includes long-lived low-throughput streaming sessions. Owner: Serving Runtime QA. ETA: 2026-01-10.

Runbook draft (on-call playbook for streaming P0/P1):
- Triage (first 5 mins):
  - Acknowledge PagerDuty; create #inc-<id>-streaming channel and add service owners
  - Post initial state and link to dashboard: Streaming -> Token emission rate, streaming-5xx-rate, per-pod RSS
  - Check recent deploys (k8s rollout history) and feature flags for streaming routes
- Quick mitigation (5–20 mins):
  - If errors + OOMs present: scale replicas x2 (k scale serving-runtime-group-<n> --replicas=<current*2>)
  - Toggle streaming aggregation feature flag off (FF: stream-agg) to test revert effect
  - If a candidate deploy within last 24h: roll back to previous stable commit (document rollback commit id)
- Deeper diagnosis (20–45 mins):
  - Inspect /metrics and per-worker logs: look for buffer allocation logs (alloc:reserve) and backpressure warnings
  - Verify nodes for memory pressure (kubectl describe nodes; check oom_kill_count)
  - If memory-driven, add mem-signal to HPA (temporary cron-based scaling as stopgap)
- Communication:
  - Post cadence updates every 10 minutes to #inc channel and update the incident doc with actions taken
  - If customer-facing SSA examples impacted, notify CS with latch on-call note and affected customers list

Runbook TODOs (to finalize):
- Add exact kubectl/CLI commands to scale and rollback (examples and safety checks)
- Standardize feature-flagging path for streaming changes (conftool + runtime API)
- Add playbook snippets for when to evacuate node/cordon and reschedule pods vs scaling

Follow-ups, owners, due dates: (flat list)
- Create streaming synthetic probe & alerts; Owner: Samir Patel; Due: 2025-11-15
- Implement memory-based autoscaling; Owner: Rina Sato; Due: 2025-11-18
- Patch allocator to use bounded pre-alloc path; Owner: Ethan Brooks; Due: 2025-11-22
- Add integration tests for long-lived streams; Owner: QA (serving-runtime); Due: 2026-01-10
- Update on-call runbook and include exact commands; Owner: Maya Gonzalez; Due: 2025-11-14
- Postmortem review session scheduled: 2025-11-14 16:00 UTC, invite: eng-sre, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api

Metrics observed (numbers rounded):
- Peak 5xx rate for streaming endpoints: 13.7% (baseline ~0.5%)
- Affected streaming sessions: ~18% of active streams (approx 9.2k of 51k live sessions)
- Incident duration: 56 minutes (14:12–15:08 UTC)
- OOM-killed pods: 3 across 2 nodes

Notes to self / informal observations: 
- The allocator change reduced short-lived allocation churn in synthetic bench runs but behaved poorly under long-lived sessions. Need to better model allocation tradeoffs.
- Feature flags and canary policy for runtime-level changes are insufficient — must create explicit canary profile that includes long-lived sessions.
- Communication: having a single incident channel helped, but CS wanted an early customer-impact summary; create a 1-line template for CS notifications next time.

Open questions:
- Why did HPA not react to memory pressure earlier? Are we missing kube metrics scraping? (investigating with infra)
- Did any downstream gateways signal TCP backoff that we didn't surface? Check ALB logs for reset patterns.

Appendix: quick links / commands (to be migrated into runbook):
- Check OOMs: kubectl get events --field-selector type=Warning | grep OOMKilled
- List recent rollouts: kubectl rollout history deployment/serving-runtime-group-4
- Toggle feature flag (runtime-admin): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://admin.redwood/api/flags/stream-agg?value=false
- Emergency rollback example: kubectl rollout undo deployment/serving-runtime-group-4 --to-revision=<n>

Status: drafts of fixes in progress; hotfix rollback verified. Please review and add any missing steps or owners.
__notes: This document is an on-drive working draft: contains triage notes, TODOs, and runbook fragments. Expect slight formatting and shorthand.
